recipes.name: Beer Braised Pork Loin
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle beer

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Heat vegetable oil a heavy pot or dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork in hot oil until brown on all sides, about 10 minutes. Remove roast from pot.
Drain all but about 3 tablespoons grease from pot. Cook and stir onion and carrots until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir beer, salt, pepper, bay leaf, and cloves into the onion mixture.
Return pork roast to the pot and cover.
Bake in the preheated oven until pork is tender and no longer pink in the center, about 2 hours.
Transfer roast to a platter and cover loosely with aluminum foil. Remove bay leaf from vegetables.

Pour the beer and vegetable mixture from the Dutch oven into a blender, filling the pitcher no more than halfway full. Hold down the lid of the blender with a folded kitchen towel and carefully start the blender, using a few quick pulses to get the vegetables moving before leaving it on to puree until smooth.
Bring pureed sauce to a boil in a saucepan over medium-high heat until thickened, stirring often, about 5 minutes. Spoon sauce over pork roast to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Beer Braised Pork Loin
raw_recipe.description: Pork loin is braised in a rich combination of beer, onion, and carrots. The veggie-beer mixture is then pureed to make a delicious gravy.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is fantastic, and the gravy at the end is just, well, GRAVY! However, we should be clear that the beer you use matters! Obviously, you should try different kinds to see what you like best, but for me this recipe was 10x better with a porter than with a Bud Lite. Also, 4 cloves was too much for my taste. two was perfect! Overall, great recipe that allows you the flexibility to make it your own! This will be a regular for my home when we entertain!

This was excellent, a great meal for a big crowd. It made gallons of gravy, which is a plus!! A couple of hints: I used a meat thermometer in the pork loin so it doesn't overcook and become dry. 170 degrees is perfectly done. I omitted the cloves (not to my taste), and when making the gravy, I threw about 1/3 cup of flour in the blender with everything else, and then cooked it all together on the stove for a few minutes to help it thicken. Delicious on mashed potatoes!

This was amazing. Both of our kids devoured it. I made it exactly as written but I cooked in a crockpot on high for 5 hours. Because of that, I skipped the step of cooking the carrots and onions in the pan. Instead, I placed them in the bottom of the crockpot and added the beer and other spices to them, stirred it up and placed the pork loin right on top to cook. After that, I followed the remaining directions that are written. Awesome meal. Served with green beans and mashed potatoes. Will definitely make again!

This was fabulous! I used a lodge Dutch oven. Two changes of note. I added an apple to the minced veggies as well as some garlic. The sauce at the end was fantastic when spooned over the thick slices of pork. Apples go well with pork.

My kids loved this, but they are not picky eaters. My gravy was thick when it came time to blend so I added some chicken stock to make more gravy and simmered it down to re-thicken. We served it over mashed potatoes and it was really good. Can't wait for my husband to eat it!

This was delicious! My 3-1/2 lb pork loin only needed an hour to cook so I think suggestions to decrease cooking time in general are correct. The gravy was fabulous and I love how it sneaked some more veggies into my kids dinners. And I’m really excited for ways to incorporate other vegetables I to it - I think any root vegetables would work easily to start.

An amazingly easy dish to cook, and for a beginner who would benefit from the 'feel' of how to braise.
I replaced carrots with butternut squash, which had been lurking at the rear of the fridge, rather than open a new bag of carrots, which would lurk
My only concern is the 'searing' process, which does tend to leave the end sections a bit harder than they should be. Perhaps these sections should not be seared...or maybe I went OTT on it.

Great dish, extremely flavorful. Lots of gravy! I would caution to watch the time on your loin in the oven. 2 hours was a little long for mine. 

I added a cup of chopped celery to my veg mix and it was heavenly. Save a few of the vegetables to spoon over the plated dinner for an added texture.
Excellent meal! Came out much better than expected. The pork was particularly tender and moist. Used parsnips instead of carrots and the sauce was very sweet. Will use this recipe again.
I made this for Xmas supper and everyone loved it! I cooked in a roaster on 250 for 5 hours. Very flavorful and tender. Thanks for sharing! Definitely a keeper in my favorite recipes. :0)

Love, love, love! Delish. Made sweet potatoes extra flavorful. Did not change a thing. Would use more bay leaf and cloves next time. I also made air fryer roasted corn on the cob. All great mix of flavors.

This was great. I had a loin just less that 3 lbs, so it was done around 1.5 hours. I added an apple as well, used a Shiner Bock beer, and added a little cumin and ginger powder. There’s not much left!
This was amazing! The gravy is the star, though, in my opinion. I reheated leftover gravy and ate it as soup. Delicious!

Oh my gosh! We loved it. Very tasty and moist. Tender. We did not use cloves; however, just not a fovorite spice for us.
This is a must make dinner!
The pork itself was very good -- moist as could be. The gravy, though, was rather sour (maybe I used the wrong beer?). Won't try it again.
Made no changes. We loved this and I will definitely make it again.
It came out quite bland and the meat was dry. I did use non-alcoholic beer and added an apple, but I don't think that made the difference. I think that braising this very lean cut was the problem
I loved it did not change any thing will make again
This was delicious! Superb way to make a great gravy that's thick and tasty!
